turns.zh: 随着你的业务成长，Vanta 也随之扩张，自动化合规，给你的安全与风险一个单一可信来源。了解更多请访问 vanta.com/invest。

turns.en: Ridgeline offers one unified platform that automates away the complexity across portfolio accounting, reconciliation, reporting, trading, compliance and more, all at scale.
turns.zh: Ridgeline 提供一个统一平台，把组合会计、对账、报告、交易、合规等等的复杂性在规模化层面全部自动化掉。

turns.en: Schedule a demo at Ridgeline.ai. Every investment firm is unique and generic AI chatbots don't understand your process. Rogu is built by finance professionals.
turns.zh: 在 ridgeline.ai 预约一次 demo。每家投资公司都是独一无二的，通用 AI chatbot 不懂你的流程。Rogo 是金融专业人士打造的。

turns.en: It's connected to your data, learns your process and quickly produces client-ready outputs. Check them out at rogu.com slash invest. The best AI and software companies from open AI to cursor to perplexity use WorkOS to become enterprise-ready overnight, not in months.
turns.zh: 它连着你的数据、学习你的流程，很快产出可以直接交付客户的成果。去看看 rogo.com/invest。最好的 AI 和软件公司，从 OpenAI 到 Cursor 到 Perplexity，都用 WorkOS，一夜之间企业级就绪，而不是几个月。

turns.en: Visit WorkOS.com to skip the unglamorous infrastructure work and focus on your product. What's the most emotional low that you faced? When we were raising our Series A, we didn't have any star investors in our cap table yet, but there was a great investor, David Tisch at Box Group, who was an early preceded seed investor, who introduced me to a bunch of all-time greats for the Series A.
turns.zh: 访问 workos.com，跳过那些不体面的基础设施工作，专注你的产品。你经历过情绪上最低的低谷是什么？我们融 A 轮的时候，股东名单上还没有明星投资人，但有一位很棒的投资人，BoxGroup 的 David Tisch，他很早就投了我们的 pre-seed 和 seed，并为了 A 轮把我介绍给一批历史上最伟大的投资人。

turns.en: And I thought, wow, I've seen what it does to get a blue chip investor in your cap table, what it does for recruiting talent, becoming more of a black hole for brand and customers and so on.
turns.zh: 我想，哇，我见过一个蓝筹投资人进股东名单会带来什么：对招募人才、对品牌和客户变成黑洞等等的作用。

turns.en: This is finally the opportunity we're going to have to do that. We've been building for two and a half years. And David introduced us to 40 investors, and I met with everybody.
turns.zh: 这次终于就是我们要做成的机会，我们已经建了两年半。David 给我们介绍了 40 家投资人，我全都见了。

turns.en: I met with Sequoia, Kleiner, Benchmark, everybody, and 40 people passed. And it wasn't just like, you get the email with the deck, and it's not exciting.
turns.zh: 我见了 Sequoia、Kleiner、Benchmark，所有人，40 家全都 pass。而且不是那种发个带 deck 的邮件、对方觉得不够兴奋就完事。

turns.en: It was like, oh, this is interesting. Let me meet Gabe. Oh, I kind of like Gabe. Let me spend an hour with him. Oh, Gabe, come to IC. Oh, Gabe, let's go to dinner.
turns.zh: 而是：哦，这有意思，我来见见 Gabe。哦，我有点喜欢 Gabe，我跟他聊一个小时。哦，Gabe，来上 IC。哦，Gabe，一起吃个晚饭。

turns.en: Oh, Gabe, come in for the weekend afterwards. You know what? We're going to pass. And it's so personal, because at that stage, it has nothing to do with anything but you, right?
turns.zh: 哦，Gabe，周末再来一趟吧。然后说：你知道吗，我们要 pass。这件事极其私人，因为在那个阶段，一切都只关于你这个人，对吧？

turns.en: It's like being broken up with by 40 girlfriends who, like, every time you fell in love, and then every time they said, eh, not for you. And that was actually Thrive, too, at the Series A.
turns.zh: 就像被 40 个女朋友甩了，每一次你都坠入爱河，然后每一次对方说：嗯，不合适。Thrive 在 A 轮也是这样。

turns.en: Thrive spent so much time with me. He went to dinner with Avery and Vince, fell in love with them and the firm, because they were awesome, and then crushing blow.
turns.zh: Thrive 和我花了很长时间。他去和 Avery、Vince 吃了饭，爱上了他们、爱上了这家公司，因为他们太棒了，然后是毁灭性的拒绝。

turns.en: And luckily, Keith Reboy came basically a month after everyone else had rejected us, and Keith was like, Gabe, this isn't a contrarian bet. It's basically just Harvey for finance.
turns.zh: 幸运的是，Keith Rabois 基本在其他所有人拒绝我们一个月之后来了。Keith 说：Gabe，这根本不是一笔逆向投资，这基本上就是金融版的 Harvey。

turns.en: Why would I do it? And I said, Keith, if it's not contrarian, why did every single one of your friends just say it was a bad idea and not believe in me?
turns.zh: 我为什么要投？我说，Keith，如果它不逆向，为什么你的每一个朋友刚刚都说这是个坏主意、都不信我？

turns.en: Why do you think they didn't believe? For a lot of reasons. I think people underappreciated the TAM and finance, which was silly, but it's partly because I think SF has less intuition for finance, because they didn't fund Ion Group or Bloomberg or S&P or Faxette or Pitchbook, Morningstar, and so on.
turns.zh: 你觉得他们为什么不信？原因很多。我觉得人们低估了金融的 TAM，这很傻，但部分原因我觉得 SF 对金融没那么强的直觉，因为他们没投过 Ion Group、Bloomberg、S&P、FactSet、PitchBook、Morningstar 这些公司。

turns.en: And so there actually haven't been great venture-backed businesses in this market. And so there's no intuition for the kind of contours of the market and how large it is.
turns.zh: 所以这个市场其实还没出过伟大的风投支持的生意，大家对市场的轮廓和体量没有直觉。

turns.en: Two is the product was terrible. And so every investor said, oh, I work in finance. Let me use it. Is it going to transform what I do? And they tried it, and it was wrong half the time.
turns.zh: 第二，产品当时很烂。每个投资人都会说，哦，我在金融工作，让我试试。它会不会改变我的工作？然后他们一试，一半是错的。

turns.en: And they go, this is never going to work. And it's like, guys, you know we're on the exponential. It's going to work in six months or 12 months or 18 months or whatever it is.
turns.zh: 他们就说，这东西永远成不了。但朋友们，你知道我们站在指数曲线上，六个月、十二个月或者十八个月它就会成。

turns.en: I'm going to figure it out. And the final reason was people didn't think I could figure it out. People didn't have enough data points of watching me chew glass and watching me figure out what the next iteration would be.
turns.zh: 我会把它搞定。最后一个原因是，大家觉得我搞不定。他们没有足够多的数据点，来看我嚼玻璃、看我一次次找出下一个迭代方向。

turns.en: Where do you think changed after that? Because now it's a who's who of captable. Well, because I met all these guys very early on. And I met them at every single round.
turns.zh: 你觉得那之后什么改变了？因为现在你们的股东名单是名人堂级别的。因为我和这些人在非常早期就认识，而且每一轮融资我都会去见他们。

turns.en: And so every time I said, hey, we're going to do this. And they said, yeah, there's no way. And then every time we would do it. And by the way, a lot of the times it would manifest in a different way.
turns.zh: 所以每次我说我们要做这件事，他们说，不可能。然后每一次我们都做到了。而且顺带说一句，很多时候它是以另一种形式兑现的。

turns.en: You would actually lose the key employee you needed. Or that actually excellent customer that you thought you were in the land totally dissipated.
turns.zh: 你甚至会丢掉最需要的那个关键员工。或者你以为稳稳拿下的那个极好的客户，突然就黄了。

turns.en: But we kept figuring out what to do and kept navigating the market. And I think when you're investing in a market like today, especially at Applied AI, where it's so turbulent, so ambiguous, you need to underwrite the founders being able to be extremely dynamic.
turns.zh: 但我们一直在找出该做什么、一直在市场里穿针引线。我觉得在今天这样的市场做投资，尤其是在应用 AI 这种极度动荡、极度模糊的领域，你承保的其实是创始人能不能极度动态。

turns.en: Why do you think there aren't more credible financial services competitors? Distribution is really hard to crack. I think it's far more a people problem on building trust and delivering value and working with these institutions, then just an engineering and product problem.
turns.zh: 你觉得为什么没有更多真正像样的金融服务竞争对手？分发真的很难破。我觉得要打进这些机构，靠的更多是建立信任、交付价值这类'人'的问题，而不只是一个工程和产品问题。

turns.en: But then there's an enormously high engineering and product burden too. The standard to execute to really crack this market, I think is pretty high.
turns.zh: 但工程和产品的门槛同样高得惊人。我认为，要真正打进这个市场需要达到的执行标准相当高。

turns.en: And I was just so lucky that a number of the early people I hired were ex-finance and just killers. And we just hired folks from internet network who worked at Goldman or Citi or Jeffries or Apollo or Aries or Blackstone.
turns.zh: 我很幸运，早期招的一批人都是金融出身，而且全是杀手。我们就从人脉网络里挖在 Goldman、Citi、Jefferies、Apollo、Ares、Blackstone 工作过的人。

turns.en: And so we had a team of people who were die hard, ambitious, curious, smart, and then just good humans. Low ego, humble, young enough to be open-minded and to want to eat class too.
turns.zh: 于是我们拥有这样一支团队：死忠、有野心、好奇、聪明，同时是好人。低 ego、谦逊，年轻到愿意保持开放，也愿意吃玻璃。

turns.en: I'm also really curious how you've dealt with technical talent and what matters in a technical person on your team and how that has evolved.
turns.zh: 我还很好奇你怎么对待技术人才，什么样的人在你的技术团队里重要，这个标准是怎么演变的。

turns.en: One intuition might be the value of domain expertise from the technical person has gone up as the ease of execution has changed a lot. You don't need to be super technical to write good code or less so than in the past.
turns.zh: 一种直觉可能是：随着执行难度发生很大变化，技术人员身上领域专长的价值上升了。写好代码不再需要像以前那么强的技术功底。

turns.en: So what is the shape of the engineering or technical team look like over time? I'm asking this again because I'm curious about thinking about other companies that want to tackle this and whatever their industry might be.
turns.zh: 那你的工程或技术团队的形状随时间是怎么变的？我再次问这个，是因为我好奇其他想攻进各自行业的公司会怎么做。

turns.en: So I would say there's definitely problems where domain expertise is increasing in value and product intuition and having more of a GM-like mindset versus an engineer-like mindset is super, super important.
turns.zh: 所以我想说，确实存在领域知识越来越值钱的场景，产品直觉、GM 式思维（而非工程师式思维）超级、超级重要。

turns.en: There are also parts of our product surface area where it's like you just need raw, great engineering talent because you're scaling things up so aggressively.
turns.zh: 也有一些产品面，你就是需要原始的、优秀的工程才华，因为你要极其激进地给系统扩容。

turns.en: But if I look at the folks in our team who have been so excellent, a lot of them are former founders. They're folks who started businesses, persevered, ate glass, had a lot of product intuition, figured out how to channel it, and then the business may be petered out.
turns.zh: 但如果我看我们团队里那些特别出色的人，很多是前创始人：创过业、扛过来了、吃过玻璃、有很强的产品直觉、知道怎么引导它，然后生意可能慢慢归于平淡。

turns.en: And to the point you made, there's been a lot of companies trying to tackle financial AI. There's been a lot of really smart product-minded, engineering-minded domain experts who have tried to tackle finance AI and we've acquired six different fledgling financial AI startups.
turns.zh: 就像你提到的那点，尝试做金融 AI 的公司有很多，有很多产品导向、工程导向、懂领域的聪明人试过金融 AI，我们已经收购了 6 家羽翼未丰的金融 AI 初创公司。

turns.en: And so those former founders who can be galaxy-brained about the future of the product and navigate a course on what the UX should be but also have engineering chops and so they can constantly make the right decisions is super important.
turns.zh: 所以那些前创始人，既能对产品的未来有 galaxy brain 级的想象力、为 UX 定方向，又有工程功底、能不断做出正确决策，这种人超级重要。

turns.en: You said earlier to me before we were recording that this is the first time that we have a major innovators dilemma in this category. Can you describe what you mean by that?
turns.zh: 录之前你跟我说，这是这个品类里第一次出现真正的创新者窘境（innovator's dilemma）。能讲讲你的意思吗？

turns.en: Yeah, well, I think for a lot of investment firms and a lot of high-finance financial services, the last 10, 20 years have been pretty good.
turns.zh: 我想，对很多投资公司、很多高端金融服务来说，过去 10 年、20 年过得相当不错。

turns.en: You can make a lot of money being a capital allocator, being an investor. It's a very hard industry to enter. And then especially if you're in private markets, your businesses have some natural momentum because when you raise a fund and another fund and another fund, it's hard to mess up the business after that.
turns.zh: 做资本配置、做投资人能赚很多钱。这是一个进入壁垒很高的行业。尤其如果你在私募市场，你的生意有某种天然的动量：募了一支基金、又一支、再一支之后，生意很难被搞砸。

turns.en: And I'm sure there's 100 people who have started funds who know it's 100 times harder than I just described. But to be fair, there hasn't been a moment and a shock to the market where every investment firm, every bank is saying, oh, wow, I need to completely rethink what I'm doing.
turns.zh: 肯定有 100 个募过基金的人知道这比我刚才描述的难 100 倍。但公允地说，从来没有一个时刻、一个对市场的冲击，让每家投资公司、每家银行都说：哇，我得彻底重新想我在做的事情。

turns.en: And now there's going to be an opportunity for hundreds of AI-native disruptors, AI-native investment firms, AI-native investment banks to attack my business model, and I need to figure out what I'm going to do now.
turns.zh: 而现在，机会属于成百上千的 AI 原生颠覆者、AI 原生投资公司、AI 原生投行，他们会进攻我的商业模式，我得想清楚我现在该怎么办。

turns.en: And there has not been an innovators' dilemma for private equity firms, for hedge funds, for investment banks in the long term. AI-native, what does that term mean to you?
turns.zh: 而对私募股权公司、对冲基金、投行来说，长期以来并没有真正的创新者窘境。AI-native 这个词对你意味着什么？

turns.en: Like, what is the definition of that? In some ways, I think it just means willing to constantly reinvent everything you're doing and being so AI-pilled that you don't worry about what's possible or what might seem completely far-fetched, but you are just charting a trajectory towards integrating this alien fundamental technology into everything that you do.
turns.zh: 它的定义到底是什么？在某种程度上，我觉得它就是愿意不断重塑你在做的一切，AI-pilled 到不去担心什么是可行的、或什么看起来荒诞不经，你只是径直地规划一条把这种外来的、基础性的技术整合进你所做一切的路径。

turns.en: And it's showing up in every part of the business and there's no part of the business that you hold sacred that is immune to being revolutionary.
turns.zh: 它体现在业务的每一个部分，业务里没有任何一部分是你供起来、免于被革命的。

turns.en: How do you do that? Like, so you're a leader in a company that's very AI-pilled that want to make sure... Do you want to do everything you guys said in Rogo?
turns.zh: 那怎么做？你领导着一家非常 AI-pilled 的公司……你们在 Rogo 说过的那些，你想全都做到吗？

turns.en: And yet, I'm sure there are areas that you're unhappy with the status of how much AI is used to do X, Y, or Z. How do you do it as a leader?
turns.zh: 我相信肯定有些地方，你对 AI 在 X、Y、Z 上被用到的程度还不满意。作为领导者你怎么推？

turns.en: Like, how do you make sure that your company keeps doing this as a practice and habit versus like a one-time or... So, I'll give you a very simple thing, which is every month I have a report that gets sent to me that shows me every one of the company, how much are they using the various different AI tools we have, both the ones we've procured, the ones we've built internally, all of these different things.
turns.zh: 你怎么让公司把它变成一种实践和习惯，而不是一阵风？我讲个非常简单的做法：每个月我都会收到一份报告，列出公司每个人对我们各种 AI 工具的使用量，包括外部采购的和内部自建的，所有这些。

turns.en: And I have a stack ranking within every division of the top five power users and the bottom five users. And we post that everywhere, and the bottom user in each division gets a printout with a dunce cap and we post it around the office.
turns.zh: 而且每个部门前五名的重度用户和后五名的用户我都做了排名。这些贴得到处都是，每个部门垫底的那位会收到一张印着傻瓜帽的打印照，贴满办公室。

turns.en: And it's hilarious, but people know it's coming. And by the way, as we get bigger and fewer people know me and know it's kind of a joke and I'm funny, they're actually terrified.
turns.zh: 这很好笑，但大家都知道会有这一出。而且顺带说一句，随着我们越来越大、和我熟、知道这是玩笑的人越来越少，他们是真的害怕。

turns.en: And I hope they're not terrified and I hope that changes, but it's a strong incentive function to actually make sure you're using these things.
turns.zh: 我希望他们别那么怕，也希望这会改变，但这是一个很强的激励函数，逼你真的把这些东西用起来。

turns.en: If you were to list questions, let's say there's someone sitting down that runs one of these firms that's been a great business, hard fought, but a great business.
turns.zh: 如果让你列一份问题清单——假设现在坐着一个经营着一把好生意的人，来之不易，但确实是好生意。

turns.en: And these businesses tend to be quite simple from an organizational and technical standpoint. It's mostly humans, right? There's not a lot of overhead in lots of these businesses.
turns.zh: 这类公司在组织和技术的角度往往相当简单，主要就是人，对吧？这些生意没什么管理开销。

turns.en: Maybe they buy a lot of data or something. What questions would you encourage them to ask of themselves, of their business, to stand the best chance of navigating this transition effectively?
turns.zh: 也许他们买很多数据。你会建议他们问自己、问自己的生意哪些问题，才能最大程度地有效穿越这次转型？

turns.en: If you knew for sure that right now 90% of your enterprise value is in your people, your best investors, your best bankers are the people that bring in deals, bring in revenue.
turns.zh: 如果你现在确定，90% 的企业价值在人身上：你最好的投资人、最好的 banker，是带来 deal、带来收入的人。

turns.en: And actually, that's what accrues enterprise value. And in 10 years, the world's best investment firms, best banks will have 90% of their enterprise value, not in people, but in software and data and systems.
turns.zh: 而企业价值实际上就是这么累积的。10 年后，世界上最棒的投资公司、最好的银行，90% 的企业价值将不在人身上，而在软件、数据和系统里。

turns.en: What would you start doing? You would start trying to figure out how do you take all of what lives in the latent minds of your best people and putting it into a system that you own and operate autonomously?
turns.zh: 你会开始做什么？你会开始琢磨：怎么把你最优秀那批人脑子里的隐性知识，装进一个你拥有、由你自主运行的系统里？

turns.en: So that's a big one. The second thing I would think about is unpack every part of the deal life cycle. And in each one, try and chart, where do you think you are invaluable or you have data or you have domain expertise that no one else has?
turns.zh: 这是个大问题。第二件我会思考的是：把交易生命周期的每一环拆开，在每一环里画出坐标：你觉得自己在哪些环节不可替代、拥有别人没有的数据、或者拥有别人没有的领域知识？

turns.en: And then be diligent about saying, okay, do I actually have something that no one else has in this market? And is it a relationship? Is it context that no one else has?
turns.zh: 然后认真地自问：在这个市场里，我真的有别人没有的东西吗？它是一段关系？是一份别人没有的上下文？

turns.en: Or do I just think I'm smarter and better read on the subject area in the market, in which case AI is going to obviate that? Have you seen anyone be the most cutting-edge exemplar of this attitude in a big firm?
turns.zh: 还是我只是自认为更聪明、对这个领域和市场更有研究——如果是后者，AI 会把这点优势抹平。你见过哪个大机构里的人成为这种态度最前卫的样板吗？

turns.en: Like, is there a favorite example of a person that's just... Oh, yeah, there's a curious thing of this. It's the folks that today look the most prescient, sounded crazy batshit two years ago.
turns.zh: 比如，有没有一个你最喜欢的人的例子？哦，有这么一件怪事：今天看起来最有先见之明的人，两年前听起来都像疯子。

turns.en: They were the guys that came in and said, we need to record every conversation. You're going to be able to pipe in this conversation directly into my company brain and there's going to be a digital clone of me and then it's going to spit out the game theory on exactly what the investment should look like.
turns.zh: 就是那些走进来说'我们要录下每一场对话。这场对话会被直接灌进公司大脑，会有我的数字分身，然后它会吐出博弈论推演，精确告诉你这笔投资该长什么样'的人。

turns.en: And two years ago, everyone listened to those kind of guys and were like, what the heck is Patrick talking about? One example is there's a co-founder of Firmolus, John Montazzi, who was just prescient about where it was going and he wanted digital clones of all their best bankers.
turns.zh: 两年前大家听到这种人说话，都会想：Patrick 到底在讲什么鬼。一个例子是 Firmolus 的联合创始人 John Montazzi，他对要去哪里极有先见之明，他想要所有最好 banker 的数字分身。

turns.en: He wanted systems that could basically show up to calls, speak on his behalf, know how he thinks and then ingest that context. And then he wanted to build a system such that anyone in junior levels of that investment bank could leverage his expertise and context and relationships immediately so that that context and that data wasn't just powering his ability to be revenue generating, but it was a powering the ability of every junior
turns.zh: 他想要那种能替他上电话会、代表他发言、懂他如何思考、然后把这些上下文吸收进来的系统。他还想建一套系统，让投行里任何初级的人都能立刻调用他的专业、上下文和人脉，让这些上下文和数据不只是支撑他一个人创造收入，而是让这个银行里每一个初级的人都能创造收入。

turns.en: in that bank to be revenue generating. And so there are a number of folks who had their kind of move 37 moment where they realized, wow, this is going to be so much more profound than anyone's expecting.
turns.zh: 所以有不少人迎来了自己的 Move 37 时刻，意识到：哇，这件事会比任何人预想的都深远得多。

turns.en: What to you feels the most uncertain about the future of your business? I would say how quickly private markets actually do transform. If you think about why different types of asset classes have increased in transaction volume and have increased in liquidity, often it has to do with standardization because it gets easier than to track those assets and trade them.
turns.zh: 对你来说，关于你生意的未来，什么最不确定？我会说，是私募市场到底能多快完成转型。想想为什么不同资产类别的交易量和流动性会上升，往往和标准化有关，因为资产的跟踪和交易变容易了。

turns.en: Private markets have been immune to standardization because there's so much unstructured data. AI should fix that. That said, is there going to be a regulatory or a market force that forces some additional standardization that really accelerates the kind of transparency and liquidity you can have in private markets?
turns.zh: 私募市场一直对标准化免疫，因为有太多非结构化数据。AI 应该能解决这一点。话虽如此，会不会有一股监管或市场力量，倒逼出额外的标准化，真正加速私募市场能拥有的透明度和流动性？

turns.en: That's a little bit out of my control. The other thing is it's still unclear to me how much alpha will be left in the human relationships. I talk about that microcap M&A.
turns.zh: 这部分不太受我控制。另一件事是，人类关系里最终会留下多少 alpha，到现在我也不清楚。我常讲微市值（microcap）M&A。

turns.en: It's very hard to imagine that if you're a small business owner and you've been building a business for 20 years and you want to make sure that if you hand that business off to someone else that you trust them, that you can shake their hand, that that can be fully automated.
turns.zh: 很难想象这样一个场景：你是一个小企业主，花了 20 年 build 一个生意，你想确保把它交给一个你信得过的人、能跟对方握握手——这种交接能被完全自动化。

turns.en: But for a lot of sponsor owned businesses or things like secondaries or private credit or GPLP secondaries, I do think it can be fully automated.
turns.zh: 但对很多 sponsor 持有的公司，或者二手份额（secondaries）、私募信贷、GP-LP 二手份额这类东西，我确实觉得可以完全自动化。

turns.en: But how long it takes for the long tail of all these small businesses, all these medium-sized businesses, that have to deal with generational turnover for them to get comfortable clicking a button to sell their business as opposed to shaking the hand to someone, that's a little up in there to me.
turns.zh: 但那些小公司、中型公司的长尾——那些要面对代际交接的——要他们愿意点一个按钮卖掉生意、而不是和人握手成交，需要多久？这一点我真心看不准。

turns.en: If you had several new young founders here with us and they were curious about how to navigate and interface with private markets investors, what would you teach them?
turns.zh: 如果现在有几位年轻的新创始人和我们在场，他们好奇该怎么和私募市场的投资人打交道，你会教他们什么？

turns.en: What would you tell them to do, to not do? My style for fundraising might not be everyone's style. I'm super direct. I'm super transparent about what I'm worried about, where I want to go, but then you have to be very headstrong on that end state.
turns.zh: 会让他们做什么、别做什么？我募资的风格未必适合每个人。我特别直接，特别透明地讲我担心什么、想去哪里，但你必须对那个终局极其坚定。

turns.en: And then I would say it's about reps and relationships and the folks who come out of nowhere and lead the Series C or the Series D are the folks that I met at the seed and then the A and then the B and the C and they passed every time for all sorts of reasons.
turns.zh: 然后我想说的是，靠的是次数和关系。那些横空出世、领投 C 轮或 D 轮的人，都是我在种子轮、然后 A 轮、B 轮、C 轮一路见过的人，每一轮他们都 pass 了，理由各种各样。

turns.en: But they gather a lot more data on me and the business. Anything that you would encourage people to not do? I think there's a lot of the fake it till you make it and you need to have the bravado and the confidence in what you're doing, even if you're not fully confident.
turns.zh: 但他们在我身上和这门生意上积累了更多的数据。有没有什么是你会劝大家别做的？我觉得有很多 fake it till you make it 的东西，你需要有那种气势和对自己所做事的信心，哪怕你并非完全确信。

turns.en: I'm a deeply paranoid, deeply insecure, deeply scared person, but you need to put on the face and say that you are confident about where you're going, even in the moments where it's the ebb and flow, it's the ebb and flow.
turns.zh: 我是一个深度偏执、深度不安、深度恐惧的人，但你必须摆出一副自信的面孔，说你对要去的方向有信心，哪怕在潮起潮落的时刻——潮起潮落就是常态。

turns.en: And I think people can misinterpret that sometimes as like they need to pretend there's something they're not. I think that's not true. You need to believe that that 5% likelihood that you can be in $100 billion business is likely.
turns.zh: 我觉得人们有时会误读这一点，以为自己得假装成并不是自己的样子。我觉得那不对。你要相信，那 5% 做成 1,000 亿美元公司的可能性是真实存在的。

turns.en: And you don't need to pretend it's 100% likely, but you should be able to delineate with very clear roadmap and strategy how it is possible that you can become $100 billion business and then have confidence that if those things play out, you will be.
turns.zh: 你也不必假装它是 100% 的概率，但你应该能用非常清晰的路线图和战略勾画出：你成为 1,000 亿美元公司是可能的，然后有信心，如果那些事情兑现，你就会成。

turns.en: Why are you scared and insecure? I'm so paranoid about everything that can go wrong. Every day it feels like you're on the knife's edge of a thousand things collapsing, and I think the reality of this sort of business building is that it's a game of compounding momentum.
turns.zh: 你为什么害怕、为什么不安？我对所有可能出错的事都偏执。每一天都像走在一千件事同时崩塌的刀尖上，而我觉得这类创业的现实是：这是一场动量复利的游戏。

turns.en: How do you do every small thing to just race a little bit faster downhill and I'm just scared the momentum will stop? Or you hit a roadblock and then you go off course and then you need to recatalyze momentum.
turns.zh: 怎么用每一件小事，让自己往下坡滑得再快一点点。我就是害怕动量停下来，或者撞上路障、偏离轨道，然后得重新点燃动量。

turns.en: And it's so clear to me how hard it is to actually build a machine that gathers momentum. So if there's any stumbling block that holds that velocity, if I wasn't constantly petrified of those moments, I wouldn't be doing everything under the sun to prepare for them.
turns.zh: 我看得太清楚了，打造一台能积累动量的机器有多难。所以如果有任何障碍会拖慢那个速度——如果我不时刻对这些时刻感到恐惧，我就不会想尽一切办法为它们做准备。

turns.en: What have we missed? Like what that you've learned about building a company like this in this era where everything feels like a jump ball? Like it feels like there's going to be a rogo or a Harvey or whatever for every place that there can be, especially where the last mile wiring is hard and it's not just going to be anthropic, it's one company to rule them all or open AI.
turns.zh: 我们漏掉了什么？关于在这样一个一切都像开放争球（jump ball）的时代打造这样的公司——感觉凡是能长出 Rogo 或 Harvey 的地方都会长出一个，尤其是最后一公里接线很难的地方，而且不会只有 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 一家通吃——关于这门生意到目前为止的体验，你觉得什么是真正重要却被我们忽略的？

turns.en: What else have we missed that you think is really important to the experience so far of building the business? I think that there are going to be businesses that solve all these problems, but the businesses that do it are going to become black holes for talent and capital and brand and they're going to be able to siphon in the resources to actually execute.
turns.zh: 还有哪些被我们忽略、你认为对建这门生意的体验真正重要的事？我认为会有公司解决所有这些难题，而做成的那些公司会变成人才、资本、品牌的黑洞，能把资源虹吸进来去真正执行。

turns.en: Because AI is an amazing tailwind, but the execution bar is higher than it's ever been too to compete and everyone is getting pulled into the big leagues and is having their welcome to the NFL moment you have to move faster and be stronger and be more resilient and agile than you ever expected and having the right team is more important than ever.
turns.zh: 因为 AI 是很棒的顺风，但竞争的门槛也是历史上最高的：每个人都被拽进大联盟，都有'欢迎来到 NFL'的时刻——你必须比你预想的更快、更强、更有韧性、更敏捷，而对的人的团队比以往任何时候都重要。

turns.en: And the right team these days is extremely, extremely expensive. And so if you can't figure out what is the strategy to become a black hole for talent and capital as quickly as possible, I do think you are far more at risk at being roadkill of a lab or a company that can.
turns.zh: 而今天对的团队极其、极其贵。所以如果你想不出一个快速成为人才和资本黑洞的战略，我真的觉得你更容易成为被某个做得到的实验室或公司碾过的路尸。

turns.en: When I do these, I always ask my favorite question last, what is the kindest thing that anyone's ever done for you? I benefited so much by having parents who were enormously kind and generous and selfless, but it showed up in such different ways for my mother versus my father.
turns.zh: 我做这类节目时总把我最喜欢的问题放在最后：别人为你做过的最善良的事是什么？我深受我父母的恩惠，他们极其善良、慷慨、无私，但母亲和父亲表达善良的方式完全不同。

turns.en: And my mother's version of kindness was no matter what I did, I was amazing and smart and could do no wrong even though growing up, that was absolutely not the case but she instilled in me the confidence to believe in myself even when you were in those low trajectories where it felt like everything was going to go sideways, 40 knows in a row, anything right, 40 knows in a row, idiot failing out, flunking out, whatever it is.
turns.zh: 我妈的善良是：不管我做了什么，我都棒、都聪明、不会犯错，尽管成长过程中根本不是那么回事。但她给了我一种自信，让我在那些低谷、感觉一切都要完蛋的时刻仍然相信自己——连续 40 个 no，任何一次，40 个 no、蠢货被刷、留级、管它是什么。

turns.en: No matter what, she acted like I was maybe the smartest person on earth. That was irrational, but you need some of that irrational confidence that comes from just undying love.
turns.zh: 无论如何，她的举止都像我是地球上最聪明的人。这是非理性的，但你需要一点那种从永恒的爱里长出来的非理性自信。

turns.en: My dad was very different. My dad, if I came home and I'd done something wrong, would see thing, could barely look at me, couldn't understand it, right?
turns.zh: 我爸非常不同。我做了错事回家，他几乎没法直视我，理解不了，对吧？

turns.en: Like he was someone who was so disciplined, so good, had such high standards. And so his version of kindness was figuring out how does he understand who I am and why I am failing at this thing and then help me.
turns.zh: 他是一个极其自律、极其优秀、标准极高的人，所以他版本的善良是：想办法理解我是谁、我为什么在这件事上失败，然后帮我。

turns.en: He would sit down and go over every detail with me even though he sometimes just couldn't even understand why I had the opportunities I had and I couldn't take advantage of them and take the time to make me better while staying true to his principles and his standards of excellence and his definitions of good too.
turns.zh: 他会坐下来陪我过每一个细节，尽管有时候他根本无法理解我为什么拥有这些机会却不加以利用。他一边花时间让我变好，一边忠于他的原则、他对卓越的标准、他对'好'的定义。
